newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council condemns killing of Greek Cypriot.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council condemns killing of Greek Cypriot.

text.p: Security Council members strongly condemned on Tuesday the recent "unjustified" killing of a Greek Cypriot civilian by Turkish Cypriot troops.

Greek Cypriot Petros Kakouli, 58, was shot to death on Sunday when he entered Turkish-controlled territory. His family said he was collecting snails. Turkish forces said he failed to stop when ordered and was shot while escaping.

"The council deeply regrets the serious incident in Cyprus which resulted in the death of an unarmed Cypriot civilian," council President Gerardo Martinez Blanco of Honduras said in a statement to reporters after closed-door consultations.
"The council condemns in the strongest terms this unjustified act that only contributes to increased tensions in the island," he said.
The statement called on the Cypriot parties to renounce violence and "avoid confrontation at all times."
The shooting was the latest in a series of incidents in Cyprus since June in which four Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot have been killed along the U.N.-manned buffer zone.
The island has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when Turkish troops landed in northern Cyprus in response to a Greek-engineered coup in Nicosia.
